Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

canregtools 0.2.11

  • ls_vars("reframe") now includes valid custom grouping dictionaries from the active project/user directory, using their names as default labels and skipping invalid files with a warning. Built-in selection routing is unchanged.

  • create_asr(), create_quality(), and create_age_rate() now complete absent age rows as zero counts within observed summary strata using the population table, preventing omitted zero-case ages from removing denominators. Explicit missing, non-finite, or negative summary counts are rejected, and ASR calculation requires coverage of all declared age groups.

  • create_asr(), create_quality(), and create_age_rate() no longer double count existing overall-sex rows in summary or population data. Missing overall rows are generated at the original stratum before grouping; inconsistent totals are rejected when male, female, and overall rows coexist.

  • cr_map() accepts multiple names in attr for data-frame batch updates, returning a named list of effective dictionaries. Batch writes preflight all inputs and targets under writer locks and roll back files on R-level errors.

  • cr_map() is the recommended interface for configuring cr_reframe() grouping mappings via attr, accepting data frames, named character vectors, and named lists. write_registry() remains available for compatibility.

  • Registry dictionaries now store typed user overrides and merge current built-in defaults on read. Legacy files are backed up on first update, retaining all old entries as overrides. Corrupt files stop updates without being overwritten; verified replacement writes and writer locks protect dictionary files. Built-in area_type exceptions now apply even without a local dictionary file, so affected urban/rural groupings can change.

  • ls_dict() now displays effective mappings and registry labels; ls_dict_files() respects project dictionary directories and excludes backups.

  • reset_dict() explicitly resets overrides, retaining a backup.

  • write_regicode() updates now take effect immediately in tidy_var(), add_labels(), and ls_vars("regicode"); label keys and types are validated.

  • write_registry() reserves the regicode dictionary for label updates, preventing accidental format replacement.

  • cr_filter() now accepts injected conditions containing function objects.

  • cr_merge() preserves optional survival cases regardless of registry order and supports further merging of already merged fbswicd objects.

  • cr_select() treats missing condition values as non-matches; its documentation clarifies that separate conditions can match different rows.

  • create_quality() now respects decimal when processing registry lists.

  • cumrate() now excludes ages at or above eage, supports partial intervals, and validates the requested age range. Cumulative rates (including those in create_asr()) may decrease compared with earlier versions, which included an extra age group.

  • cr_filter() now interprets year as integers in direct numeric comparisons and numeric %in% conditions, while preserving character comparisons and stored year labels. Period or invalid labels produce a warning in numeric comparisons.

  • get_stdpop() now includes the 1976 and 2013 European Standard Populations and the 2000 U.S. Standard Population.

  • ls_vars("std") now lists the added European and U.S. standard populations.

  • cr_select() now avoids repeating the full cleaning pipeline when selecting registries by summary or population metrics.

  • count_canreg() now benefits from faster standard-code handling during case cleaning; classification results and non-standard sex labels are unchanged.

  • compare_mv(), compare_mi(), and compare_rate() now calculate each stratum in vectorized form instead of repeatedly slicing one-row data frames.

  • compare_rate(), cr_test(), and detect_anomaly() now interpret rate variances on the displayed scale by default. Set variance_scale = "unmultiplied" for legacy variance inputs.

  • create_asr() now extracts age-standardization results from list-columns without a rowwise data-frame pass.

  • create_asr() now constructs optional variance, standard-error, and confidence-interval columns only when requested, reusing one variance extraction when both show_var and show_se are enabled.

  • create_asr() gains show_se to return crude- and age-standardized-rate standard errors. show_var now returns variance on the same displayed rate scale, so sqrt(var) directly gives the corresponding standard error.

  • create_asr() now reports missing or non-positive population denominators with registry and age-group context, and skips invalid registries when calculating a collection.

  • create_quality() avoids sorting an intermediate case table that is sorted again in the final output.

  • create_age_rate() uses vectorized row sums for wide-format totals.

  • cr_reframe() now reuses computed registry-group indices and avoids an intermediate selection pass for each output group.

  • cr_merge() now batches component binding in cmerge(), reducing repeated per-registry data-frame copies while preserving source identifiers.

  • count_canreg() now aggregates incidence and mortality rows in one grouped pass instead of joining separately summarized tables.

  • count_canreg() now supports a batch strategy for canregs, cleaning case tables once across registries while retaining strategy = "registry" for compatibility checks; batch mode does not emit a progress bar.

  • as_fbswicd() constructs one fbswicd or registry-split fbswicds directly from summary, population, optional site/morphology, and exclusion data frames. Only fbs is required among statistic columns; omitted mortality and quality counts remain absent rather than being filled with zeros. Optional sitemorp and exclude components are omitted when NULL; explicitly supplied zero-row data frames are retained.

  • cr_combine() now combines collections of fbswicds by registry name, including minimal incidence-only objects and sparse optional components.

  • Added validate_fbswicd() for summary-level objects and collections. It checks component schemas, non-negative counts, duplicate strata, population coverage, registry identifiers, and optional site/morphology components.

  • create_site_morp() now distinguishes an unavailable sitemorp component from an explicitly supplied zero-row component.

  • calc_age() now extracts date components once per date vector, reducing case-cleaning time while preserving calendar-age and missing-value semantics.

  • count_canreg() now marks duplicate IDs with vectorized operations instead of grouping each ID, retaining the existing non-missing duplicate counts.

  • cr_clean() now accepts numeric text in population count columns, preserves missing optional death counts, and reports the exact variable and stratum for invalid population values. Population denominators (rks) remain strict.

  • ageadjust() now returns finite Gamma bounds for zero-event rates under all interval methods, validates inputs, and correctly derives missing counts or populations from rates. Fractional case totals are no longer rounded.

  • as_canreg() now applies year to separate inputs too: diagnosis years for incidence and death years for mortality. Population rows remain unchanged.

  • count_canreg() now retrieves excluded mortality identifiers from SWcases.

  • cr_merge() now gives merged canreg objects a scalar identifier and retains original identifiers in source_regicodes, satisfying registry validation.

  • Dictionary storage can be isolated with options(canregtools.dict_dir = ...). Tests now use temporary dictionaries instead of modifying user configuration.

  • cr_clean() now matches population by age-group codes, supports standard 18- and 19-group schedules, preserves fractional totals and empty inputs, and rejects incomplete or duplicated schedules instead of replacing them with zeros.

  • truncrate() now excludes the group beyond the inclusive upper age limit and rejects boundaries that do not align with complete age groups.

  • expand_age_pop() now falls back to non-negative linear interpolation when a cubic interpolation method would overshoot below zero.

  • benchmark_age_split() now supports blind validation against an independent single-age schedule, reporting MAE, RMSE, total variation, ASR bias, source-group conservation, negative values, and available uncertainty diagnostics.

  • classify_icd10() now supports the 63-category CI5-XII cancer classification (cancer_type = "ci5"), with site codes from 401 through 461 and the shared aggregate codes 60 and 61.

  • tidy_var() cancer labels now use consistent CI5/IARC English terminology, standardized ICD-10 range notation, and corrected full-name and abbreviation fields across the cancer classification tables.

  • expand_age_pop() now accepts arbitrary source_breaks, preserves the final open age group, and enforces non-negative, exact effective source-group totals. It adds reference-schedule allocation, Sprague for regular closed five-year groups, and optional PCLM through ungroup.

  • expand_open_age_pop() now provides a separate high-age module that either retains the open group or uses an external high-age reference schedule while retaining a final open group.

  • get_stdpop() now returns standard-population weights for requested age groupings, using exact aggregation by default and opt-in interpolation only when a requested boundary splits an original group. create_asr() uses this mechanism when input age groups differ from the default structure.

  • create_asr() now accepts 18 five-year age groups with age 0 included in the 0–4 group, combining the corresponding standard-population weights automatically.

  • compare_rate() and cr_test() now support CI5-style statistical tests of incidence or mortality rate differences using rate variances.

  • Added ci5_xii_china, a pooled China incidence reference from CI5-XII with registry-level ASR audit data. CI5-XII/XIId do not contain the death or diagnosis-basis fields required for MI or MV references, so those components are explicitly marked unavailable.

  • compare_mi(), compare_mv(), and cr_test() can now use an external reference table instead of the other registries in the target data.

  • Added detect_anomaly() for uncertainty-based consecutive-year and robust historical-level screening of annual rates and quality indicators returned by create_asr() and create_quality().

  • Registry identifiers now use regicode throughout canreg and fbswicd workflows, including comparison, validation, reports, and bundled dictionaries. This breaking change replaces areacode; arbitrary character identifiers are supported, while classify_areacode() remains specific to Chinese six-digit administrative codes.

  • compare_mi() is added to test each registry’s mortality-to-incidence ratio against other registries in the same stratum.

  • compare_mv() is added to test each registry’s morphologically verified percentage against other registries in the same stratum.

  • count_canreg() now retains cases with missing IDs while excluding them from duplicate-case counts.

  • count_canreg() now identifies canreg components by name, so its result no longer depends on their list order.

  • cr_combine() is added to combine multiple canregs objects by registry name.

  • cr_select() can now filter canregs and fbswicds by population-year count and range.

  • cr_test() now provides a unified entry point for the M:I and MV% quality tests.

  • create_quality() now reports rates and proportions with a zero denominator as missing rather than zero.

  • Improved package metadata in DESCRIPTION, including a more informative package description, author ORCID, and affiliation.

  • year and sex are now character identifiers throughout canreg, fbswicd, bundled data, and derived workflows. Population years accept single calendar-year labels and inclusive "YYYY-YYYY" period labels; period labels remain intact in results. detect_anomaly() remains limited to single calendar years because it evaluates consecutive annual values.

  • Updated CRAN submission metadata and removed the unused VignetteBuilder field to avoid CRAN check notes when no package vignette is provided.

  • validate_canreg(), validate_cases(), and validate_population() now provide structured, row-level data-quality checks before analysis.

  • classify_areacode() now uses the updated area-code classification implementation with attr support and custom dictionaries; classify_areacode2() has been merged into classify_areacode().

  • create_site_morp() is added for counting ICD-10 site-code and morphology-code frequencies by user-defined strata.

  • cr_reframe() again applies the registry dictionary for strat = "registry", while preserving arbitrary identifiers that cannot be classified.

  • cr_rename() renames selected registries in canregs and fbswicds objects while synchronizing their internal regicode values.

  • read_canreg() now uses readxl as an optional dependency, reducing required package dependencies when Excel import is not needed.

  • as_canreg() can now split incidence, mortality, and population data by a specified registry-code column and return a canregs object.

  • as_canreg() now uses the shorter inci, mort, and pop argument names.

  • write_registry() now validates registry mappings, preserves built-in defaults when refreshing, and returns the updated dictionary for inspection.

canregtools 0.2.9

  • Fixed an issue where mortality rates were not displayed when incidence rates were missing for certain cancer types.
  • Corrected a calculation error in the m8000 statistics.

canregtools 0.2.8

  • Initial submission to CRAN.
